main_text.p: Constr. חֲרֵי עָפָר In foraminibus vel cavernis terrae, Job. 30.6. Aff. חָרְיוֹ Foramina sua, Nah.2.12. בְּחָרִיהֶן In foraminibus suis, Zach.14.12. Et cum Schurek, הָאָז בְּחוּרִים Illaqueando in foraminibus, Jesa.42.22. Porrò חֹר per Synecdochen speciei est Podex, Foramen ventris posterioris, unde excrementa exeunt: inde per metonymiam, חֹרִים Excrementa, appellatione obscaenâ. Ubi ergo hoc sensu vocabulum hoc occurrit, ibi Scribae legendum substituerunt aliud vocabulum in auribus honestius, cujus vocales praecedenti voci subjecerunt: ut, לְאָכְלָ אֶת־חָרְאֵיהֶם Ad comedendum excrementa sua, Jesa.36.12. quod legendum צוֹאָתָם Egesta sua, quae vox in margine posita est. Juxta consonas autem legendum fuisset חָרְאֵיהֶם vel חָרְיֵהֶם nam א advenititium. Vide infra in פּחוֹר.

חֹרוֹת f.p. Latrinae, loca ubi excrementa deponuntur. Et haec vox pronunciatu obscaena: unde alienae vocales ipsi adjectae, & alia vox, cujus vocales ista propriae, pro ea legitur, quae idcirco ad marginem posita: ut, וַיֵּשִׁיכְהוּ לְמֹחְרַאוֹת Et disponebant illud in latrinas, 2.Reg.10.27. legendum, לְמוֹצָאוֹת, quae vox תֹּר נקיה יותר honesta & pura magis, ut Hebraei ajunt. Singulare esset מָחוֹר, forma מָעוֹן.

חָרִיוֹנִים m.p. Excrementa columbarum, 2.Reg.6.25. Vox composita, & similiter obscaena. Juxta consonas essent duae voces חֲרֵי יוֹנִים Excrementa columbarum: At quia & hic חֹרִיִּם obscaenum, ut in antecedentibus, ideò legendum substituerunt in margine דְּבִיּוֹנִים, de qua vide דב. Ita prisci Hebraeorum, honestati, in legendo & pronunciando Verbo Dei sancto, consulere voluerunt, ut quae vocabula in communi & profano usu obscaena, in re sacra aures cujusquam non offenderent. Hinc Traditio, quae legitur in Cod. Talmudico Megilla, cap.3.in fine. כָּל הַמִּקְרָאוֹת הַכְּתוּבִין בְּתוֹרָה לִגְנַאי קוֹרִין אוֹתָן לִשְׁבַח : Id est, Omnes voces[?].

page.notes: The last word of the page, printed as "voces," at the foot, is partly cut off in the scan and read as "voces" with [?]. Hebrew and Greek are transcribed from the scan with vowel points as far as they are visible; points on the small letters in the entries are uncertain and may differ from the printed text. The top centre running head is a Hebrew letter sequence, read as חף. The Hebrew of several forms (e.g. לְמֹחְרַאוֹת, חָרִיִּם) is doubtful at the level of individual points and should be checked against the original. No margin notes are printed on this page.
